title: Sunny and the Busy Bee | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka finds a solitary native bee asleep inside a flower that has closed for the night, wrapped in petals and pollen and completely at peace, and realises even the busiest creatures need to stop. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The flower was closed.

Sunny bent down to look at a banksia rose that had shut its petals for the night, folding itself up like a little fist. And as she looked very closely, she saw something inside the closed petals — something small and still.

A bee.

A tiny native bee, tucked inside the closed flower. Asleep. Coated in pale yellow pollen — its whole body dusted with it — legs folded, not moving at all. Just resting, wrapped in petals, completely at peace.

Sunny sat back on her heels.

She had always thought of bees as the busiest creatures in the bush. Always moving. Always collecting. Always somewhere to be. And here was one, bundled up in a flower, completely still.

She thought about all the flowers the bee had visited that day. All the pollen it had collected. All the distance it had flown — and that tiny body, built for work, now taking the rest it had earned.

The pollen on its fur would become something. Somewhere a flower would bloom because of what this bee had carried.

She thought: even the hardest workers have to stop.

She sat in the soft grass beside the closed flower.

The bee slept on inside its petal room.

Sunny closed her eyes too.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, busy bee. Goodnight, little one.
